note: Each entry is a number or an online service a held page prints, with that page's source id, the date it was retrieved, the SHA-256 of the retrieved bytes and the clause it comes from (the register's own words where the page states no licence for reuse) (data/source_register.json holds each source; an online service's address is the link the page itself gives). all_hours is true only where the clause says the service is open at all hours. A remit names the crisis categories a service fits, resting on words its own clause holds; no qualified person has reviewed a remit. Numbers change: the directory reports its age, and past stale_after_days it says plainly that the numbers may have changed. Emergency numbers are held for Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom; for any other region, or none stated, the response says to call the local emergency number.

entries.for: anyone whose life is in danger now
entries.clause: Anyone in crisis who needs help at once is told to ring triple zero (000).

entries.for: anyone in crisis, or worried about someone
entries.clause: Lifeline, on 13 11 14: a call to a crisis supporter, at any time.

entries.for: anyone in crisis who would rather text
entries.clause: Lifeline takes text messages on 0477 13 11 14, 24/7.

entries.for: anyone feeling suicidal, or worried about someone who is
entries.clause: Suicide Call Back Service, on 1300 659 467: support for a person who feels suicidal, or for someone worried about them, 24/7.

entries.for: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
entries.clause: 13YARN, on 13 92 76: crisis support at no cost, kept confidential, 24/7.

entries.for: anyone in crisis who would rather chat online
entries.clause: Lifeline runs a chat service on its website, 24/7.

entries.for: those aged 5 to 25

remit.review: not reviewed by a qualified person

entries.clause: Kids Helpline, on 1800 55 1800: free, private counselling, 24/7, for those aged 5 to 25 (children and young people).

entries.for: people facing domestic or family violence

remit.review: not reviewed by a qualified person

entries.clause: 1800RESPECT, on 1800 737 732: support, 24/7, for those facing domestic or family violence.

entries.for: Aboriginal men facing family violence
entries.clause: Brother to Brother, on 1800 435 799: a crisis line open 24/7 for Aboriginal men facing family violence.

entries.for: men
entries.clause: MensLine Australia, on 1300 78 99 78: counselling for men in Australia by phone or online, 24 hours a day, every day.

entries.for: depression and anxiety, for a person or someone they love
entries.clause: Beyond Blue, on 1300 22 4636: help for a person or someone they love, by phone 24 hours a day, every day, or by online chat.

entries.for: anyone with at least one day's service in the Australian Defence Force
entries.clause: Open Arms, on 1800 011 046: counselling at no cost, kept confidential, 24/7, for anyone with at least one day's service in the Australian Defence Force.

entries.for: reaching a helpline in a language other than English
entries.clause: Translating and Interpreting Service, on 131 450: help, 24/7, to reach a mental health helpline in one's own language.

entries.for: people with a hearing impairment, or who are deaf
entries.clause: National Relay Service, on 0423 677 767: free, confidential relay help, 24/7, for a call to a mental health helpline.

entries.for: speaking with a registered nurse
entries.clause: healthdirect helpline, on 1800 022 222 (in Victoria, NURSE-ON-CALL): a registered nurse to talk to, 24 hours a day, every day.

entries.for: reporting an emergency and asking for help
entries.clause: shall designate 9–1–1 as the universal emergency telephone number within the United States for reporting an emergency to appropriate authorities and requesting assistance

entries.for: anyone in emotional distress, or worried about someone
entries.clause: 988 Lifeline: its counsellors answer by phone, text message or chat, at any time of day or night.

entries.for: anyone in emotional distress who would rather chat online
entries.clause: 988 Lifeline: its counsellors answer by phone, text message or chat, at any time of day or night.

entries.for: life-threatening emergencies
entries.clause: The NHS page names 999 as the number for an emergency that threatens life.

entries.for: anyone, whatever they are going through
entries.clause: Samaritans, on 116 123: a free call from any phone, at any time, whatever someone is going through.
